sentences: I fill the hanging feeder with black oil sunflower seeds each morning before the sun rises.
I scrub the bird bath with a brush and replace the water to remove algae and debris.
I count the house finches and chickadees that land on the platform feeder within ten minutes.
I watch a robin gather dry grass and twigs to build a cup nest in the maple tree.
I open the wooden nest box and record the number of blue eggs resting on the pine shavings.
I aim the microphone at the wren and save its repeated song to my laptop's audio folder.
I hold the sparrow gently and stretch its wing against a ruler to measure the length.
I place the warbler in a small cloth bag and hang it from the digital scale to get its weight.
I wrap the parrot in a towel and clip the sharp tips of its overgrown talons with nail clippers.
I lift the soiled paper from the bottom of the canary cage and lay down a fresh sheet.
I attach a calcium-rich cuttlebone to the side of the budgie's cage near the water dish.
I collect the small feathers that fall from the cockatiel and note which wing they came from.
I log the dates when the Canada geese fly south over the field behind my house.
I use binoculars to compare the red head and gray body of the woodpecker on the trunk.
I part the feathers under the pigeon's wing and look for moving mites with a magnifying glass.
I raise the wooden perch in the finch aviary by two inches to match the new feeder height.
I mash boiled egg yolk with a fork and place the mixture in a shallow dish for the lovebirds.
I check the incubator's thermometer and write down the temperature reading for the chicken eggs.
I fit a small aluminum band around the cardinal's leg and close the metal ring with pliers.
I pick up the stunned thrush from the patio floor and place it in a dark box to recover.
